channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: KKR Wraps Up $2.1 Billion Leveraged Loan for Integer Acquisition
item.description: KKR & Co. Inc. finalized a $2.1 billion loan to help fund its pending acquisition of medical-device maker Integer Holdings Corp. after securing more-favorable terms, seizing on investor demand for leveraged-buyout financings.
item.dc:creator: Jeannine Amodeo

item.title: Jon Ledecky reflects on Sept. 11 and NYC sports scene
item.description: Jon Ledecky, NHL team New York Islanders co-owner, sat down with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to remember the events on Sept. 11, the power of sports and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Finding Stability in Investing: Masters in Business with Seth Bernstein
item.description: Barry speaks with Seth Bernstein, Chief Executive Officer of AllianceBernstein. They discuss his tenure at JPMorgan Chase where he was managing director and global head of Managed Solutions & Strategy at J.P. Morgan Asset Management. They discuss understanding the Private Credit industry and the future of Mutual Funds as ETFs become the future of investing. Seth also discusses the importance of in-person collaboration as well as how to invest for retirement. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bill Dudley Expects Fed to Raise Rate by 25 Bps
item.description: Bill Dudley, a Bloomberg Opinion columnist and former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, says he would be shocked if the Federal Reserve did not raise interest rates by 25 basis points at their next meeting. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan’s GPIF May Sell $62 Billion of Treasuries, Santander Says
item.description: Japan’s Government Pension Investment Fund could sell as much as $62 billion of US Treasuries without a formal revamp of its asset-allocation policy, according to analysts at Banco Santander SA.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie

item.title: AI-Obsessed Wall Street Pours Billions Into Inflation-Era Bets
item.description: The list of challenges confronting Wall Street piled up this week. Oil firmly above $100. Inflation refusing to disappear. A defiant bond market that all but dared Scott Bessent to bring more policy firepower.
item.dc:creator: Vildana Hajric and Isabelle Lee

item.title: CFTC Clears Faster Payouts for Tipster Awards Under $5 Million
item.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission plans to automatically award successful whistleblowers 30% of any enforcement penalties collected if a tipster is due to receive $5 million or less, the agency said Friday.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: Saudi East-West Pipeline Shut Down as Precaution After Attack
item.description: Bloomberg's Veena Ali-Khan said that clashes between Houthi rebels and Saudi Arabia is an 'escalation' of regional tensions as fighting disrupts key areas for oil production. Ali-Kahn said that Saudi Arabia is caught between a rock and a hard place when it comes to responding to recent attacks, as leaders weigh the impact of military retaliation against gains in leverage for the Houthis. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: National Guard Presence a 'Significant Investment' In DC Safety, Says Brig. Gen. Blanchard
item.description: Brigadier General Leland Blanchard II, Interim Commanding General of the DC National Guard, said that safety efforts in the 25 years since the September 11th terrorist attacks have been a balance between honoring personal liberties and the need for security. Brigadier General Blanchard also discussed his current mandate with the National Guard in DC and how his team works in coordination with the DC police, saying that it represents a 'significant investment' in the security of DC neighborhoods. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Scores of Young Sports Fans Placed Their First Bets This Summer
item.description: Bloomberg's Zijia Song joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." This summer’s FIFA World Cup packed stadiums across North America and drew record audiences. It also got a large number of millennials and Gen Zs to place their first sports bets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Must Think Of Wealth Transfers Differently: Zentner
item.description: Ellen Zentner, chief economic strategist and global head of thematic and macro investing at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how wealth managers must adjust to people living longer. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wealth Transfers Are Happening Later: Zentner
item.description: Ellen Zentner, chief economic strategist and global head of thematic and macro investing at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss financial planning, retirement, and the impact of growing life expectancy in the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Should 'Deeply Value' Friendship of It's Allies, Says Former NATO Ambassador
item.description: Nicholas Burns, former Ambassador to NATO, reflected on the 25th anniversary of the September 11th and remembered the action of NATO countries in the days following the terror attacks, saying the US should 'deeply value' the friendship of its allies. Burns who also served as the US ambassador to China previewed the issues on the table ahead of President Xi's upcoming visit to the US and said the US, China and NATO allies 'need to be together in limiting the influence of AI when it comes to weapons of mass destruction.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oraclum Hedge Fund Founder Charged With Lying About Returns
item.description: Vuk Vukovic, a founder of New York hedge fund Oraclum Capital LLC, was charged by federal prosecutors with lying to investors about his fund’s performance.
item.dc:creator: Bob Van Voris and Chris Dolmetsch

item.title: Dollar Wavers as CPI Adds to Fed Hike Bets While Oil Falls
item.description: The dollar oscillated Friday after a key gauge of US consumer prices rose by more than expected, pushing traders to add to bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week.
item.dc:creator: Anya Andrianova

item.title: Treasuries End Bruising Week With Fed Hike Bets Firmed After CPI
item.description: The $32 trillion US bond market ended a bruising week that pushed yields to multiyear highs, with investors more convinced the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week to address sticky inflation.
item.dc:creator: Ye Xie and Greg Ritchie

item.title: Stocks Rise as Attention Shifts to Next Week’s Fed Rate Decision
item.description: US stocks rallied as retreating oil prices offered relief following a report showing accelerating core inflation, which led traders to boost bets the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates next week.
item.dc:creator: Felice Maranz

item.title: Lululemon’s Newest Bear Sees More Pain Ahead After 81% Rout
item.description: Lululemon Athletica Inc.’s turnaround won’t be a quick or easy fix as the athletic wear company cedes market share to rivals and suffers deepening sales declines, according to BMO Capital Markets, which initiated coverage of the stock this week with an underperform rating.
item.dc:creator: Peyton Forte

item.title: Stocks Climb in Run-Up to Next Week’s Fed Decision: Markets Wrap
item.description: The final stretch of a jittery week on Wall Street saw stocks rising, with a decline in oil prices tempering concerns about inflationary pressures ahead of next week’s Federal Reserve decision.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 11
item.description: Brent oil dipped Friday but gained significantly overall for the week as the Iran war and threats against Saudi Arabia from Houthi militants keep traders on edge.
item.dc:creator: Bingyan Wang, Mia Gindis and Alex Longley
